subject.title: Expose the active config revision over the Gateway protocol

question: Should the Gateway adopt a canonical resolved-config revision contract and expose both saved and actively applied revisions in `config.get` and the hello snapshot?
rationale: The feature is useful and additive, but maintainers must choose permanent public semantics for what is hashed and exactly when the running revision advances across startup, hot reload, no-op, rejection, and restart paths.

options.title: Approve canonical dual revisions
options.body: Define one resolved revision algorithm, expose saved and applied hashes in both protocol surfaces, and keep the existing raw hash as the write guard.

options.title: Expose through config.get only
options.body: Keep the handshake smaller and require clients to call `config.get` after connecting or reconnecting to reconstruct applied state.

options.title: Defer runtime revision tracking
options.body: Keep browser-local pending state and accept that out-of-band restarts cannot be reconstructed truthfully.

recommendation.title: Approve canonical dual revisions
recommendation.body: Define one resolved revision algorithm, expose saved and applied hashes in both protocol surfaces, and keep the existing raw hash as the write guard.

likelyOwner.reason: They proposed the contract and have the strongest available history signal on the central Gateway configuration documentation.
